dialogue.text: You got your Abitur! I knew you'd find it.
So... are you really leaving us?
Good luck out there, son. Make us proud.
Take your time, dear. We'll be here.
Martin! You forgot your Abitur again, didn't you?
It's still at the Otto-Hahn-Gymnasium, over by the university. Go get it before someone frames it.
The world is big, Martin.
Where will you go first?
Good choice. The Black Forest will treat you well.
You'll figure it out. You always do.
Little brother! Four years younger and still can't bench your own laptop.
Deadlines? I only know deadlifts.
I'd tell you a lifting joke, but it's too heavy for you.
Your code needs more core strength. Get it? Core?
Squat. Bench. Commit. In that order.
Moving to Freiburg? Don't worry, I'll carry the boxes. It counts as cardio.
Rest days are for people who finished their reps.
I was nine when you were born. I've been cleaning up after you ever since.
Now you're the one taking computers apart. At least you put them back together these days.
Go. Study. Call Mom on Sundays.
Ten years older than you, and I still remember changing your diapers.
And now you're leaving. Promise you'll write?
You better! I'll hold you to it.
That's not very reassuring...
Get in, the Mercedes is warmed up. Well, it's warm. It's always warm. The heater is stuck.
So, what's the plan this morning?
Sure, sure. We'll drive past the café on the way. Just to look.
The correct answer. Lectures get recorded in our hearts.
Freiburg. Chair of Software Engineering. Bring your proofs, and a warm jacket.
Hello, Martin. I hear you like making computers do what they're told.
If you want to get out of here, you have to do a PhD.
Excellent. Come to Freiburg. We will prove programs correct. Or at least doomed.
Then enjoy Saarbrücken. The door isn't going anywhere. Neither are you.
Customers now look at stairs on a screen and nod. I have never been so respected.
A woman asked if the software also does ladders. I told her ladders are just stairs with commitment issues.
Your program is the only software I have ever understood. I do not understand it, but I respect it.
Is that it? The stairs... on the screen... turning?
People will see their stairs before they climb them. That is almost philosophy.
Here. Your first paid software job. Spend it on something with a railing.
The stairs are waiting. They are very patient, but they are not getting any younger. Did you talk to Ben?
Martin. Serious question, for once.
I sell stairs at Bickelmann. Beautiful stairs. But nobody can imagine them before they're built.
You do computers. Could you write a program that shows people their staircase?
Wonderful. You'll need help. Doesn't your friend Ben do 3D?
Pity. The stairs will remain unimaginable. Like most things.
I've decided to only eat food whose name works backwards. Yesterday I had a Semmel. Lemmes. Very good.
Do you think staircases get lonely at night? Nobody goes up at three in the morning. Only down.
A man on the bus told me a cardigan is just a jacket that has something to confess. I believe him.
I once sorted my socks alphabetically. Then I learned socks don't have names. It was a difficult week.
We shipped software to a real customer. We should put that on a business card.
Valentin paid us and then told me a story about a sad umbrella for twenty minutes. Worth it.
Rendering is done. Spiral staircases look amazing, the straight ones look... straight. Go show Valentin.
Valentin wants software that shows his stairs in 3D? Before anyone builds them?
It's 2003. Nobody has done that for a stair shop. We'd be pioneers. Pioneers of stairs.
Deal. I'll do the rendering, you do the logic. Meet you back at Valentin's.
Exams are forever. Stairs are also forever. Tough call.
You missed the Operating Systems class this morning. Again.
Did you finish the compiler construction assignment? My parser rejects everything, including itself.
The Mensa has schnitzel today. That's the whole announcement.
The exam is on Thursday. Or Tuesday. It's definitely on a day.
Can I copy your lecture notes? Oh right. You were at brunch with Evren.
Another one? Better not. You've got a train to catch eventually.
Best bug-hunting team in the Saarland. Put it on your CV.
You got all of them! My apartment is bug-free for the first time since... ever.
That calls for a beer. Karlsberg?
Prost! (The Saarland gets a little wobbly.)
More for me. Offer stands.
{bugsLeft} {bugsNoun} still on the loose. Last seen near the university and the steelworks.
Martin! Some bugs escaped from my apartment. They don't bite. They're just... everywhere.
Can you squash them? Walk up to one and press Z (or tap the Z button) to swing.
There are {bugsLeft} of them. Get them all and I'll buy you a beer.
